zajjaj:72-72.t:
His words: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلى ما جاءَنا مِنَ البَيِّناتِ والَّذِي فَطَرَنا﴾ — the position of ”اَلَّذِي“ is genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: ”لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلى اللَّهِ“ ("we will never prefer you over Allah"). It is also possible for ”اَلَّذِي“ to be genitive as an oath, the meaning then being: ”لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلى ما جاءَنا مِنَ البَيِّناتِ واللَّهِ“ ("we will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us — by Allah!"), i.e. ”نَحْلِفُ بِاللَّهِ“ ("we swear by Allah").
His words: ﴿فاقْضِ ما أنْتَ قاضٍ﴾, i.e. ”اِصْنَعْ ما أنْتَ صانِعٌ“ ("do whatever you are going to do"). Abū Dhuʾayb said:
؎وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(On the two of them were two chain-mail coats that David had fashioned — or Tubbaʿ, maker of the ample coats of mail.)
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّما تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ — the reading is with the accusative: ”اَلْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا“. It would be permissible [grammatically] to say ”إنَّما تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الحَياةُ الدُّنْيا“ with the nominative, its interpretation being that what you decree is [merely] the enjoyment of the life of this world; but I do not know of anyone who read it with the nominative.
And His words: ﴿وَما أكْرَهْتَنا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 73] — the position of ”ما“ is accusative; the meaning is: ”لِيَغْفِرَ لَنا خَطايانا وإكْراهَكَ إيّانا عَلى السِّحْرِ“ ("that He may forgive us our sins and your compelling us to sorcery"). It is related that Pharaoh compelled them to learn sorcery. The meaning of ﴿واللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وأبْقى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 73] is: ”اَللَّهُ خَيْرٌ لَنا مِنكَ وأبْقى عَذابًا“ ("Allah is better for us than you, and more lasting in punishment"), because they said this to him in reply to his words: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أيُّنا أشَدُّ عَذابًا وأبْقى﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 71].

zajjaj:77-77.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فاضْرِبْ لَهم طَرِيقًا في البَحْرِ يَبَسًا﴾ — ”يابِسًا“ is also possible, as is ”يَبْسًا“ with a sukūn on the bāʾ. Whoever says ”يابِسًا“ makes it a naʿt (adjective) of the road; whoever says ”يَبَسًا“ describes it with the maṣdar (verbal noun), the meaning being: ”طَرِيقًا ذا يَبَسٍ“ ("a road possessing dryness"). One says: ”يَبِسَ الشَّيْءُ، يَيْبَسُ، ويَيْبِسُ، يَبَسًا، ويُبْسًا، ويَبْسًا“ ("the thing became dry") — three dialectal forms of the maṣdar.
And His words: ﴿لا تَخافُ دَرَكًا ولا تَخْشى﴾ — ”لا تَخَفْ دَرَكًا ولا تَخْشَ“ is also possible. Whoever reads ”لا تَخافُ“, the meaning is: ”لَسْتَ تَخافُ دَرَكًا“ ("you are not one who fears being overtaken"); whoever says ”لا تَخَفْ دَرَكًا“, it is a prohibition against fearing, and its meaning is: ”لا تَخَفْ أنْ يُدْرِكَكَ فِرْعَوْنُ، ولا تَخْشَ الغَرَقَ“ ("do not fear that Pharaoh will overtake you, and do not dread drowning").

zajjaj:78-78.t:
﴿فَأتْبَعَهم فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ﴾ — it is also read ”فاتَّبَعَهم فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ“. Whoever reads ”فَأتْبَعَهُمْ“, there is in it evidence that he pursued them with the troops along with him. Whoever reads ”فاتَّبَعَهم فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ“, its meaning is: ”ألْحَقَ جُنُودَهُ بِهِمْ“ ("he sent his troops after them to catch them up"); according to this wording it is possible that he was with them and possible that he was not — except that he was in fact with them.
﴿فَغَشِيَهم مِنَ اليَمِّ ما غَشِيَهُمْ﴾: ”اَلْيَمُّ“ is the sea, and the meaning is: ”فَغَشِيَهم مِنَ اليَمِّ ما غَرَّقَهُمْ“ ("there covered them of the sea that which drowned them").

zajjaj:81-81.t:
And His words: ﴿وَلا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكم غَضَبِي ومَن يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوى﴾ — it is also read: ”فَيَحُلَّ عَلَيْكم غَضَبِي، ومَن يَحْلُلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي“. Whoever reads ”فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ“, its meaning is: ”فَيَجِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ“ ("so that it becomes due upon you"); whoever reads ”فَيَحُلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ“, its meaning is: ”فَيَنْزِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ“ ("so that it descends upon you"). The reading ”وَمَن يَحْلِلْ“ with a kasra on the lām is more common.
﴿فَقَدْ هَوى﴾, i.e. he has perished and gone down to al-Hāwiya, which is the bottom of the Fire of Hell.

zajjaj:82-82.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنِّي لَغَفّارٌ لِمَن تابَ وآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدى﴾, i.e. ”تابَ مِن ذَنْبِهِ، وآمَنَ بِرَبِّهِ، وعَمِلَ بِطاعَتِهِ“ ("repented of his sin, believed in his Lord, and acted in obedience to Him"). ﴿ثُمَّ اهْتَدى﴾, i.e. ”ثُمَّ أقامَ عَلى إيمانِهِ“ ("then remained steadfast in his faith").

zajjaj:84-84.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ هم أُولاءِ عَلى أثَرِي﴾ — ”أُولاءِ“ is indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra. ”عَلى أثَرِي“ belongs to the ṣila (relative clause) of ”أُولاءِ“. It may also be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as though He said: ”هم عَلى أثَرِي هَؤُلاءِ“. The better view is that it is a ṣila.
It has been transmitted as ”أُولايَ عَلى أثَرِي“, but there is no justification for it, because a yāʾ does not come final after an alif except for annexation, as in ”هُدايَ“. I know of none of the well-known Qurʾān readers who read it so; al-Farrāʾ mentioned it, and there is no justification for it.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
His words: ﴿فَإنّا قَدْ فَتَنّا قَوْمَكَ مِن بَعْدِكَ﴾, i.e. We cast them into a trial (fitna) and an ordeal, and We tested them.
﴿وَأضَلَّهُمُ السّامِرِيُّ﴾ — some of the exegetes said: ”اَلسّامِرِيُّ“ was a non-Arab boor (ʿilj) from the people of Kirmān. Most of the exegesis holds that he was one of the great men of the Children of Israel, from a tribe known as al-Sāmira, who to this day are known in Syria (al-Shām) as the Samaritans (al-Sāmiriyyūn).

zajjaj:86-86.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿غَضْبانَ أسِفًا﴾ — ”أسِفٌ“ means intensely grieved, together with his anger.
And His words: ﴿أنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكم غَضَبٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ — the reading here is with a kasra on the ḥāʾ of ”يَحِلَّ“, in the sense that it becomes due upon you; the ḍamma is also permissible in it, in the sense of ”أنْ يُنْزِلَ عَلَيْكم غَضَبٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ“ ("that anger from your Lord should descend upon you").

zajjaj:87-87.t:
﴿قالُوا ما أخْلَفْنا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنا﴾ — the ḍamma, the kasra and the fatḥa are all permissible on the mīm: ”بِمَلْكِنا“, ”بِمُلْكِنا“ and ”بِمِلْكِنا“. The basic sense of ”اَلْمُلْكُ“ is authority and power; ”اَلْمِلْكُ“ is what the hand possesses; and ”اَلْمَلْكُ“ is the maṣdar (verbal noun): you say ”مَلَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ، أمْلِكُهُ، مَلْكًا“ ("I owned the thing").
It is said in some of the exegesis: ”ما أخْلَفْنا مَوْعِدَكَ بِأنْ مَلَكْنا الصَّوابَ“ ("we did not break our appointment with you because we were in control of what was right"). It may also mean: ”ما أخْلَفْنا مَوْعِدَكَ بِسُلْطانٍ كانَ لَنا، ولا قُدْرَةٍ“ ("we did not break our appointment with you through any authority or power we had"). Then they told the reason for their failing to keep to him, saying: ”وَلَكِنّا حَمَلْنا أوْزارًا مِن زِينَةِ القَوْمِ“. It is also read ”حُمِّلْنا أوْزارًا“, with the mīm doubled and given a kasra. By ”اَلْأوْزارُ“ they mean ornaments they had taken from the people of Pharaoh when the sea cast them out and threw them onto its shore, so they took the gold and the silver. They were called ”أوْزارًا“ because its meaning is "sins" (”اَلْأثامُ“). It is also possible that they were called ”أوْزارًا“ meaning "burdens" (”أثْقالًا“), because ”اَلْوِزْرُ“ in the language is a load, and sin was called ”وِزْرًا“ because the one who commits it has been loaded with a weight by it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ﴾ [al-Sharḥ: 2] ﴿الَّذِي أنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ﴾ [al-Sharḥ: 3].
So they said: ”حَمَلْنا حُلِيًّا، فَقَذَفْناها في النّارِ، وكَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ السّامِرِيُّ“ ("we carried ornaments and threw them into the fire, and so did the Sāmirī"), i.e. he threw in ornaments he had with him.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
﴿فَأخْرَجَ لَهم عِجْلا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوارٌ﴾ — there is disagreement over the interpretation of its lowing (khuwār). It was said that it would low as a bull among animals lows; when it lowed they would prostrate to it, and when the lowing came again they would rise from prostration. Some said it lowed only a single time, and their evidence is: ﴿أفَلا يَرَوْنَ ألا يَرْجِعُ إلَيْهِمْ قَوْلا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 89]. Mujāhid said: its lowing was the rustling of the wind when it entered its hollow inside.
It is related that Hārūn (Aaron), peace be upon him, passed by the Sāmirī while he was making the calf and said to him: ”ما تَصْنَعُ؟“ ("What are you making?"). He said: "I am making what neither benefits nor harms," and he said: "Pray [for me]." So Hārūn said: ”اَللَّهُمَّ أعْطِهِ ما يَسْألُ كَما يُحِبُّ“ ("O Allah, give him what he asks as he wishes"). So he asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, to give the calf a lowing.
What Mujāhid said — that its lowing was the rustling of the wind in it — is more readily accepted, because it is something possible. The other interpretation — namely, that it was a lowing made possible as a trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in that He tested the people with it — [is also possible]. [Translator's note: the Arabic sentence breaks off without an explicit predicate here; the bracketed words are supplied for sense.] There is nothing in the lowing of brass that necessitates worshipping it, since they had seen it made and fashioned; so their worship of it — even if it had lowed and spoken as a human speaks — would not have been made obligatory by that.
﴿فَقالُوا هَذا إلَهُكم وإلَهُ مُوسى فَنَسِيَ﴾ — it was said that the Sāmirī forgot the faith he had been upon, because he became a hypocrite when he crossed the sea; the meaning is: ”فَتَرَكَ ما كانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الإيمانِ“ ("so he abandoned the faith he had been upon"). It was also said that the Sāmirī told them: Mūsā (Moses), peace be upon him, wanted this calf, but he forgot, and missed the way that leads to it.

zajjaj:89-89.t: And His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أفَلا يَرَوْنَ ألا يَرْجِعُ إلَيْهِمْ قَوْلا﴾ — just as He said: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا أنَّهُ لا يُكَلِّمُهم ولا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلا﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 148]. ”ألّا يَرْجِعَ“ is also permissible, accusative through ”أنْ“; but the preferred usage with ”رَأيْتُ“, ”عَلِمْتُ“ and ”ظَنَنْتُ“ is ”أنْ لا يَفْعَلُ“ (with the indicative), in the sense of ”قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أنَّهُ لا يَفْعَلُ“ ("I know that he does not do").

zajjaj:94-94.t:
And His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قالَ يا ابْنَ أُمَّ لا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي ولا بِرَأْسِي﴾ — ”يا ابْنَ أُمَّ“ with a fatḥa on the mīm, or if you wish ”يا ابْنَ أُمِّ“ with a kasra on the mīm. ”أُمَّ“ was given a fatḥa although its position is genitive, because ”اِبْنَ“ and ”أُمَّ“ were made into a single noun, so ”اِبْنَ أُمَّ“ was made indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. Whoever says ”يا ابْنَ أُمِّ“ annexes it to himself [the speaker]. There is a third possibility: ”يا ابْنَ أُمِّي لا تَأْخُذْ“, but it is not read so, since the yāʾ is not written in the muṣḥaf. An example of this from poetry:
؎يا ابْنَ أُمِّي ويا شُقَيِّقَ نَفْسِي أنْتَ خَلَّيْتَنِي لِدَهْرٍ شَدِيدِ
(O son of my mother, O dear brother of my soul, you have left me to a hard fate.)
This [fatḥa construction] has come only in ”اِبْنَ أُمِّ“ and ”اِبْنَ عَمِّ“. That is because ”يا ابْنَ أُمَّ“ is said to someone who is not a brother through the mother, nor a brother at all; likewise ”يا ابْنَ عَمِّ“ is said to a stranger. So when it was removed from its proper category it was made indeclinable on the fatḥa. And even if a speaker also says ”يا ابْنَ أُمَّ“ to his brother through his mother, he has merely included his brother among those to whom he says ”يا ابْنَ أُمَّ“. It has been said of Hārūn that he was not Mūsā's brother through his mother — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:95-95.t: His words: ﴿قالَ فَما خَطْبُكَ يا سامِرِيُّ﴾ — the meaning of ”ما خَطْبُكَ؟“ is: ”ما أمْرُكَ الَّذِي تُخاطِبُ بِهِ؟“ ("what is this affair of yours about which you are being addressed?").

zajjaj:96-96.t:
﴿قالَ بَصُرْتُ بِما لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ﴾ — one says ”قَدْ بَصُرَ الرَّجُلُ، يَبْصُرُ“ when he has knowledge of a thing, and ”أبْصَرَ، يُبْصِرُ“ when he looks. The interpretation is: ”عَلِمْتُ بِما لَمْ يَعْلَمُوا بِهِ“ ("I knew what they did not know"). He had seen the horse of Jibrīl (Gabriel), peace be upon him, and took a handful of the dust from the horse's hoof[print]. One says ”قَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً“ and ”قَبَصْتُ قَبْصَةً“ with the undotted ṣād: the qabḍa is with the whole palm, and the qabṣa is with the fingertips. It is read with both the ṣād and the ḍād.
There is another form in it, which to my knowledge has not been read: ”فَقَبَصْتُ قَبْصَةً، وقُبْصَةً“ is permissible [in the language], but reading with it is not permissible if it has not been read. The qabṣa is taking hold of a thing once, and the qubṣa is the amount that is taken hold of. Comparable to this are His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إلا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً بِيَدِهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 249] and ”غَرْفَةً بِيَدِهِ“.
﴿فَنَبَذْتُها﴾: I threw it into the calf so that it would low. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِي نَفْسِي﴾, i.e. my soul made it seem attractive to me; and similar to it is: ﴿الشَّيْطانُ سَوَّلَ لَهم وأمْلى لَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 25].

zajjaj:97-97.t:
﴿قالَ فاذْهَبْ فَإنَّ لَكَ في الحَياةِ أنْ تَقُولَ لا مِساسَ﴾ — also ”وأنَّ لَكَ“. ”لا مَساسِ وأنَّ لَكَ“ is also possible, with a fatḥa on the mīm and a kasra on the final sīn, on the pattern of ”دَراكِ“ and ”تَراكِ“. The interpretation is that Mūsā, peace be upon him, forbade mixing with the Sāmirī, so the meaning is: ”إنَّكَ في الدُّنْيا لا تُخالَطُ جَزاءً لِفِعْلِكَ“ ("in this world you will not be mixed with, as a recompense for your deed").
Whoever reads ”لا مِساسَ“ with a fatḥa on the final sīn, it is accusative as the head of [the lā] construction [Translator's note: the Arabic «مَنصُوبٌ عَلى البَدْءِ بِهِ» is literally "accusative on the basis of beginning with it", i.e. as the noun of the lā of generic negation]. Whoever says ”لا مَساسِ“, it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, and it is a negation. Your saying ”مَساسِ“ means: ”مَساسِ القَوْمِ تَأْمُرُ بِذَلِكَ“ ("touch the people!" — you command that), so when you say ”لا مَساسِ“ it is the negation of that. ”مَساسِ“ was made indeclinable on the kasra, though its basic vowel would be the fatḥa because of the alif; but ”مَساسِ“ and ”دَراكِ“ are feminine, so the kasra was chosen for the meeting of two quiescent letters, because in the feminine you say ”فَعَلْتِ يا امْرَأةُ“ ("you did, O woman") and ”أعْطَيْتُكِ يا امْرَأةُ“ ("I gave you, O woman").
﴿وَإنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ﴾ — also ”لَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ“. Whoever reads ”لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ“, the meaning is: ”يُكافِئُكَ اللَّهُ عَلى ما فَعَلْتَ في القِيامَةِ، واللَّهُ لا يُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ“ ("Allah will requite you for what you did at the Resurrection, and Allah does not break the promise"). Whoever reads ”لَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ“, the meaning is: ”إنَّكَ تُبْعَثُ، وتُوافِي يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ، لا تَقْدِرُ عَلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ، ولَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ“ ("you will be raised and will arrive on the Day of Resurrection; you are not able to do otherwise, and you will not miss it").
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وانْظُرْ إلى إلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عاكِفًا﴾ — also ”ظِلْتَ“, with a fatḥa and a kasra on the ẓāʾ. Whoever gives it a fatḥa, its base form is ”ظَلِلْتَ“, but the lām was elided because of the heaviness of the doubling and the kasra, and the ẓāʾ remained with its fatḥa. Whoever reads ”ظِلْتَ“ with the kasra transferred the kasra of the lām onto the ẓāʾ. This [elision] may also occur in what does not have a kasra, as in ”أحَسْتُ“ meaning ”أحْسَسْتُ“; and ”هَمْتُ بِذَلِكَ“ has been reported, meaning ”هَمَمْتُ“. The meaning of ”عاكِفٌ“ is "staying, remaining devoted"; ”عاكِفًا“ is accusative as the khabar (predicate) of ”ظَلْتَ“; it is not accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And His words: ﴿لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ — it is also read ”لَنُحْرِقَنَّهُ“, i.e. we will burn it with fire; when it is doubled, the meaning is: ”نَحْرِقُهُ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ“ ("we will burn it time after time"). It has also been read ”لَنَحْرُقَنَّهُ“, and its interpretation is: we will file it down with a file; one says ”حَرَقْتُ، أحْرُقُ، وأُحْرِقُ“ when I file a thing. ”لَنُحْرِقَنَّهُ“ has not been read, but if it were read it would be permissible. [Translator's note: the text earlier gives ”لَنُحْرِقَنَّهُ“ as a reading and here says it has not been read; this is translated as written — the intended form in one of the two places may differ in its vowelling.]
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ في اليَمِّ نَسْفًا﴾ — ”اَلْيَمُّ“ is the sea, and ”اَلنَّسْفُ“ is scattering [in the wind].

zajjaj:101-101.t: And His words: ﴿وَساءَ لَهم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ حِمْلا﴾ — the meaning is: ”ساءَ الوِزْرُ لَهم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ“ ("evil is the burden for them on the Day of Resurrection"), and ”حِمْلًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:102-102.t:
﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ﴾ — its explanation has already been given earlier. Most of what the lexicographers hold is that ”اَلصُّورُ“ is the plural of ”صُورَةٌ“ ("form").
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ المُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ — it was said: thirsty; and it was said: blind — they come out of their graves seeing, as they were created the first time, and become blind at the place of gathering. It was said ”زُرْقًا“ ("blue") only because the black [of the eye] turns blue when their sight goes. Whoever says "thirsty" is also good, because from the severity of thirst the black of their eyes changes until it turns blue.

zajjaj:103-103.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَتَخافَتُونَ بَيْنَهم إنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إلا عَشْرًا﴾ — the basic meaning of ”اَلْخُفُوتُ“ in the language is stillness, and ”اَلتَّخافُتُ“ here is speaking secretly; so the meaning is that they whisper secretly among themselves.

zajjaj:104-104.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْثَلُهم طَرِيقَةً﴾, i.e. the most knowledgeable of them, in his own estimation, of what he says. ﴿إنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إلا يَوْمًا﴾ — its meaning is: ”ما لَبِثْتُمْ إلّا يَوْمًا“ ("you remained only a day").

zajjaj:105-105.t:
And His words: ﴿فَقُلْ يَنْسِفُها رَبِّي نَسْفًا﴾ — ”اَلنَّسْفُ“ is scattering: the mountains become like scattered dust, blown and scattered about.
﴿فَيَذَرُها قاعًا صَفْصَفًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 106] — ”اَلْقاعُ مِنَ الأرْضِ“ is the place over which water rises; it is also said: the good [level] place. ”اَلصَّفْصَفُ“ is level ground.

zajjaj:107-107.t: ﴿لا تَرى فِيها عِوَجًا ولا أمْتًا﴾ — ”اَلْعِوَجُ“ in a stick or a mountain is its not being straight, and ”اَلْأمْتُ“ is that one place is thick and another thin.

zajjaj:108-108.t:
His words: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ الدّاعِيَ لا عِوَجَ لَهُ﴾ — the meaning is: ”لا عِوَجَ لَهم عَنْ دُعائِهِ“ ("they have no swerving from his call"); they are unable not to follow.
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلا تَسْمَعُ إلا هَمْسًا﴾ — ”اَلْهَمْسُ“ in the language is something faint and hidden, and ”اَلْهَمْسُ“ here, in the exegesis, is the sound of the treading of feet.

zajjaj:110-110.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وما خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — ”ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ“ is the matter of the Resurrection and all that is to be, and ”ما خَلْفَهُمْ“ is what has already taken place of their deeds.

zajjaj:111-111.t: And His words: ﴿وَعَنَتِ الوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ القَيُّومِ﴾ — the meaning of ”عَنَتْ“ in the language is "they humbled themselves"; one says ”عَنا، يَعْنُو“ when he submits. From it is said ”أُخِذَتِ البِلادُ عَنْوَةً“ ("the lands were taken by force") when they were taken by conquest and taken with the submission of their people.

zajjaj:112-112.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلا يَخافُ ظُلْمًا ولا هَضْمًا﴾ — ”اَلْهَضْمُ“ is diminution. One says ”فُلانٌ يَهْضِمُنِي حَقِّي“, i.e. he diminishes my right for me; likewise ”هَذا شَيْءٌ يَهْضِمُ الطَّعامَ“ ("this is something that digests food"), i.e. it diminishes its heaviness.

zajjaj:113-113.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَلَّهم يَتَّقُونَ أوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهم ذِكْرًا﴾, i.e. perhaps the threat will produce in them a remembrance of the punishment and so restrain them from acts of disobedience. It was also said: ”أوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهم ذِكْرًا“, i.e. honour.

zajjaj:114-114.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَعْجَلْ بِالقُرْآنِ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يُقْضى إلَيْكَ وحْيُهُ﴾, i.e. before its explanation is made clear to you. It is also read: ”مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَقْضِيَ إلَيْكَ وحْيَهُ“ with the nūn. ”مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَقْضِيَ إلَيْكَ وحْيَهُ“ is also permissible, i.e. ”مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ إلَيْكَ وحْيَهُ“ ("before Allah completes His revelation to you"), but ”يَقْضِيَ“ has not been read; what has been read is ”يُقْضى“ and ”نَقْضِي“, with the yāʾ and the nūn.

zajjaj:115-115.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنا إلى آدَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ ولَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا﴾ — ”فَنَسِيَ“ here means "so he abandoned [it]", because one who forgets is not held to account for his forgetting. It has come in the ḥadīth: «"If the forbearance of the children of Adam, from the time of Adam until the Hour is established, were weighed, the forbearance and resolve of all whom he begot would not equal the forbearance and resolve of Adam ﷺ"; and He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا﴾».

zajjaj:119-119.t:
And His words, Glorified is He: ﴿وَأنَّكَ لا تَظْمَأُ فِيها ولا تَضْحى﴾ — both ”وَإنَّكَ“ with the kasra and ”وَأنَّكَ“ with the fatḥa are permissible. If you use the kasra, it is resumptive, the conjoining of one sentence to another. If you use the fatḥa, it is in the sense of ”إنَّ لَكَ ألّا تَظْمَأُ فِيها“, so you conjoin ”أنَّكَ“ to ”ألّا تَجُوعَ“; and on this view ”أنَّكَ“ is in the position of the accusative. It may also be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the noun of ”إنَّ“ [as a whole], with ”أنَّ“, because the meaning of ”إنَّ زَيْدًا قائِمٌ“ is ”زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“ ("Zayd is standing"); so the meaning is: ”ذَلِكَ أنَّكَ لا تَظْمَأُ فِيها“ ("and that you will not thirst in it").
The meaning of ”لا تَظْمَأُ“ is "you will not be thirsty"; one says ”ظَمِئَ الرَّجُلُ، يَظْمَأُ، ظَمَأً، فَهو ظَمْآنُ“, meaning thirsty. The meaning of ”وَلا تَضْحى“ is: the sun will not strike you, and you will not be exposed; one says ”ضَحى الرَّجُلُ، يَضْحى“ when he is exposed to the sun. The poet said:
؎رَأتْ رَجُلًا أمّا إذا الشَّمْسُ عارَضَتْ فَيَضْحى وأمّا بِالعَشِيِّ فَيَخْصَرُ
(She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, is exposed to its heat, and in the evening is pierced by the cold.)
The meaning of ”يَخْصَرُ“ is: khaṣar strikes him, which is severe cold and its reaching the extremities.

zajjaj:124-124.t:
And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن أعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا﴾ — the basic meaning of ”اَلضَّنْكُ“ in the language is narrowness and hardship. Its meaning — and Allah knows best — is that this straitened life is in the Fire of Hell; but most of what has come in the exegesis is that it is the punishment of the grave.
And His words: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ أعْمى﴾ is like ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ المُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 102]. It was also said: blind to his argument; its interpretation is that he has no argument to which he could find his way — not that he has an argument and is blind to it. People have no argument against Allah after the messengers; to Allah belongs the conclusive argument, and He has given glad tidings and warned, promised and threatened.

zajjaj:126-126.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ كَذَلِكَ أتَتْكَ آياتُنا فَنَسِيتَها وكَذَلِكَ اليَوْمَ تُنْسى﴾, i.e. ”كَذَلِكَ تُتْرَكُ في النّارِ، كَما تَرَكْتَ آياتِنا“ ("thus you are left in the Fire, just as you left Our signs").

zajjaj:128-128.t:
And His words: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهم كَمْ أهْلَكْنا﴾ — it has been read with the nūn and with the yāʾ. Whoever reads with the nūn, its meaning is: ”أفَلَمْ نُبَيِّنْ لَهم بَيانًا يَهْتَدُونَ بِهِ؟“ ("have We not made clear to them an explanation by which they may be guided?"). Whoever reads ”أفَلَمْ يَهْدِ“ with the yāʾ, the meaning is: ”أفَلَمْ يُبَيَّنْ لَهُمُ الأمْرُ بِإهْلاكِ مَن قَبْلَهم مِنَ القُرُونِ؟“ ("has the matter not been made clear to them by the destruction of the generations before them?"). ”كَمْ“ is in the position of the accusative, governed by ”أهْلَكْنا“.
Quraysh used to trade and would see the dwellings of ʿĀd and Thamūd bearing the marks of destruction; that is His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ في مَساكِنِهِمْ﴾. ”فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ“ is also permissible, i.e. in the place of their dwelling, but it has not been read. It is also read ”يُمَشَّوْنَ في مَساكِنِهِمْ“, with the doubling.
And His words: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآياتٍ لأُولِي النُّهى﴾, i.e. for those possessing intellect and understanding. One says ”فُلانٌ ذُو نُهْيَةٍ“ when he has an intellect by which he refrains from vile deeds.

zajjaj:129-129.t: And His words: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ لَكانَ لِزامًا﴾, i.e. the killing that befell them would have been binding forever, and the punishment would have clung to them. ﴿وَأجَلٌ مُسَمًّى﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ”كَلِمَةٌ“; the meaning is: ”لَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ وأجَلٌ مُسَمًّى لَكانَ لِزامًا“ ("were it not for a word that preceded and an appointed term, it would have been binding"). By the appointed term is meant that Allah promised them the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and that is His saying: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46].

zajjaj:130-130.t: And His words: ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وقَبْلَ غُرُوبِها﴾ — that is the time of the early morning and the evening. ﴿وَمِن آناءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وأطْرافَ النَّهارِ﴾ — ”اَلْآناءُ“ are the hours, and the singular of ”اَلْآناءُ“ is ”إنْيٌ“; we have explained it earlier. ”فَسَبِّحْ وأطْرافَ النَّهارِ“: and ”أطْرافُ النَّهارِ“ ("the ends of the day") are the ẓuhr (noon) and the ʿaṣr (afternoon). ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضى﴾ — it is also read ”تُرْضى“.

zajjaj:131-131.t:
And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إلى ما مَتَّعْنا بِهِ أزْواجًا مِنهُمْ﴾, i.e. [certain] men among them. ﴿زَهْرَةَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ — and ”زَهَرَةَ“: both, with a fatḥa on the hāʾ and with a sukūn on it. ”زَهْرَةَ“ is accusative by the sense of ”مَتَّعْنا“, because its meaning is: ”جَعَلْنا لَهُمُ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا زَهْرَةً“ ("We made the life of this world a splendour for them").
﴿لِنَفْتِنَهم فِيهِ﴾, i.e. so that We make that a trial for them.

zajjaj:133-133.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالُوا لَوْلا يَأْتِينا بِآيَةٍ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ — its meaning is: ”هَلّا يَأْتِينا بِآيَةٍ مِن رَبِّهِ؟“ ("why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?"), although the clear proofs and signs had come to them; but they sought to propose themselves whatever signs they wanted.

zajjaj:134-134.t: And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَذِلَّ ونَخْزى﴾ — ”يُذَلُّ ويُخْزى“ is permissible in it.

zajjaj:135-135.t: And His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَن أصْحابُ الصِّراطِ السَّوِيِّ﴾ — ”مَن“ is in the position of the nominative, and ”فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ“ cannot govern it, because its meaning is the meaning of equalization (taswiya); the meaning is: ”فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ أصْحابُ الصِّراطِ السَّوِيِّ نَحْنُ أمْ هُمْ“ ("you will come to know: are the people of the even path we or they?"). So ”فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ“ did not govern, because the wording of the speech is the wording of a question. The meaning of ”أصْحابُ الصِّراطِ السَّوِيِّ“ is: the people of the straight way. It is also permissible to say ”مَن أصْحابُ الصِّراطِ السُّوى ومَنِ اهْتَدى“, i.e. ”فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَن أصْحابُ الطَّرِيقَةِ السُّوءى ومَنِ المُهْتَدِي“ ("they will come to know who are the people of the evil way and who is the rightly guided").

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "Ṭā Hā" is Meccan.
﷽
His saying: ﴿طه﴾ ﴿ما أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ القُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 2]. It is read "طَـهَ", with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and the hāʾ; it is read "طِـهِ", with kasra on both; it is read "طَـهْ", with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and the hāʾ quiescent; and "طَـهِ", with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ.
There is disagreement about its interpretation. The authorities on the language said: it is one of the openings of the sūras, like "حـم" and "الـم". And it is related that the Prophet ﷺ, when he prayed, would raise one foot and put down the other, so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — sent down "طاها", that is: "Tread (طَإ) the ground with both your feet."

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَعَلِّي آتِيكم مِنها بِقَبَسٍ أوْ أجِدُ عَلى النّارِ هُدًى﴾: "اَلْقَبَسُ" is what you have taken of fire on the end of a stick or the end of a wick. ﴿أوْ أجِدُ عَلى النّارِ هُدًى﴾: it has come in the tafsīr that he ﷺ had lost the way; and it has come that he had lost [the way to] water; so he hoped to find at the fire someone who would guide him to the way or direct him to water.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿فَلَمّا أتاها نُودِيَ يا مُوسى﴾ ﴿إنِّي أنا رَبُّكَ﴾ [Ṭāhā: 12]: it is read "أنِّي أنا" — with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads "أنِّي", the meaning is: "He was called with [the words]: that I am your Lord", and the position of "أنِّي" is accusative. Whoever reads "إنِّي أنا رَبُّكَ" with kasra, the meaning is: "He was called: O Mūsā, indeed I am your Lord."
﴿فاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إنَّكَ بِالوادِ المُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 12]: it is related that he was ordered to take them off because they were of the skin of a dead (unslaughtered) donkey; and it is related that he was ordered to take them off so that he might tread the holy valley with his feet; and it is related that it was sanctified twice.
And His saying: ﴿طُوًى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 12] is the name of the valley. Four forms are permissible in it: "طُوى" with ḍamma on its first letter, without tanwīn and with tanwīn; and with kasra on its first letter, with tanwīn and without tanwīn. Whoever gives it tanwīn [takes it as] the name of the valley, and it is masculine, named with a masculine on the pattern "فُعَلٌ", like "حُطَمٌ" and "صُرَدٌ". Whoever does not give it tanwīn has made it a diptote for one of two reasons: one is that it is diverted (maʿdūl) from "طاءٍ", so that it becomes like "عُمَرُ", diverted from "عامِرٌ"; the other is that it is a name for the plot of ground (البُقْعَة), as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فِي البُقْعَةِ المُبارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 30]. If it is given kasra and tanwīn, "طِوًى", it is like "مِعًى" (intestine) and "ضِلَعٌ" (rib), fully declined; and whoever does not give it tanwīn has made it a name for the plot of ground.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَأنا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾: it is also read "وَإنّا اخْتَرْناكَ" (and We have chosen you). Whoever reads "وَإنّا اخْتَرْناكَ", the meaning is conveyed by "وَأنّا اخْتَرْناكَ"; and "وَإنّا اخْتَرْناكَ" is permissible on two aspects: as a resumption (istiʾnāf), and in the sense of reported speech (ḥikāya), because the meaning it conveys is: "It was said to him: We have chosen you."
[Translator's note: the wording of the first sentence is as in the source; the intended contrast is evidently between «وَأنّا اخْتَرْناكَ» (with fatḥa, conjoined to ﴿أنِّي أنا رَبُّكَ﴾) and «وَإنّا اخْتَرْناكَ» (with kasra).]

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾: this has two meanings. One of them is: "Establish prayer so that you remember Me", because prayer does not take place without remembrance of Allah. The second meaning is the one that people hold, and its meaning is: "Establish prayer whenever you remember that a prayer is due from you, whether you are within its time or not", because Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — does not take us to task if we forget, so long as we have not deliberately pursued things that occupy and distract from prayer. If someone remembers that a prayer is due from him at the time of sunrise or at sunset, he must pray it. And it has been read "لِلذِّكْرى"; its meaning is: at the time of your remembering.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنَّ السّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أكادُ أُخْفِيها﴾, with ḍamma on the alif [i.e. the hamza]. It has come in the tafsīr: "I almost hide it from Myself"; and Allah knows best the reality of this interpretation. It has been read "أكادُ أخْفِيها", with fatḥa on the alif; its meaning is: "I almost reveal it." Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎فَإنْ تَدْفِنُوا الدّاءَ لا نَخْفِهِ وإنْ تُوقِدُوا الحَرْبَ لا نَقْعُدِ
(If you bury the malice, we will not bring it out; and if you kindle war, we will not sit back.)
That is: if you bury the malice, we will not reveal it. This second reading is clearer in meaning, because the meaning of "I almost reveal it" is: "I have hidden it, and I almost revealed it."
And His saying: ﴿لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى﴾: the meaning of "بِما تَسْعى" is: by what it does. "لِتُجْزى" is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying: "إنَّ السّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى" (the Hour is coming so that every soul may be requited for what it strives for). It may also be on [the sense]: "أقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي لِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما تَسْعى" (establish prayer for My remembrance, so that every soul may be requited for what it strives for).

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْها مَن لا يُؤْمِنُ بِها﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: let not one who does not believe in it turn you away from affirming it, that is: one who does not believe that it will come about. The address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to the whole of his community; the meaning of "لا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْها" is "لا يَصُدَّنَّكُمْ" (let him not turn you [all] away). Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]: He drew the Prophet's ﷺ attention by the address, and he and his community were addressed by His saying ﴿إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1].
And His saying: ﴿فَتَرْدى﴾: its meaning is "and you perish". One says "رَدِيَ، يَرْدى، رَدًى" when he perishes; and likewise "تَرَدّى" when he perishes, in His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مالُهُ إذا تَرَدّى﴾ [al-Layl: 11].

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يا مُوسى﴾: "تِلْكَ" is a vague noun (ism mubham, i.e. demonstrative) which is treated like "اَلَّتِي" (the one which) and takes a ṣila (relative clause) just as "اَلَّتِي" does; the meaning is: "What is that which is in your right hand, O Mūsā?"
This speech has the wording of a question, and its function in speech is that of something asked about, to which the addressee answers by acknowledging it, so that the proof is established against him after he has acknowledged; his acknowledgement makes it unnecessary [to argue], so that he cannot deny after the proof has occurred. Its like in speech is that you show the addressee water and say to him: "What is this?" He says: "Water." Then you change it with some dye; and if he says, "It has always been like this," you say to him: "Did you not acknowledge that it is water?"

zajjaj:18-18.t:
And His saying: ﴿هِيَ عَصايَ أتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْها﴾: it has also been read "هِيَ عَصَيَّ", without alif. The better of the two is "عَصايَ"; "عَصَيَّ" is the dialect of Hudhayl. The rule for the yāʾ of the first-person possessive is that what precedes it takes kasra: you say "هَذا حَجَرِي" (this is my stone), giving the rāʾ kasra though it is in the position of ḍamma, and likewise "رَأيْتُ حَجَرِي" (I saw my stone). But when it comes after the short alif (alif maqṣūra), you do not give it kasra, because the alif does not take a vowel; likewise when it comes after the alif of the dual in the nominative, in your saying "هُما غُلامايَ" (they are my two servants), and after the yāʾ of the accusative, in your saying "رَأيْتُ غُلامَيَّ" (I saw my two servants), and after every yāʾ preceded by a kasra, such as "هَذا قاضِيَّ" (this is my judge) and "رَأيْتُ مُسْلِمِيَّ" (I saw my Muslims). So Hudhayl, instead of [giving] the alif a kasra, changed it into yāʾ. There is none of the grammarians who has not reported this dialect. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
؎سَبَقُوا هَوَيَّ وأعْنَقُوا لِهَواهُمُ فَتَخَرَّمُوا ولِكُلِّ جَنْبٍ مَصْرَعُ
(They outran my desire and hastened to their own fate, so they were carried off; and for every side there is a place of falling.)
His saying: ﴿وَأهُشُّ بِها عَلى غَنَمِي﴾: it has come in the tafsīr: "I beat down leaves from the trees with it." Its derivation is from [the idea] that I bring the thing to brittleness (هَشاشَة) and ease [of falling].
And His saying: ﴿وَلِيَ فِيها مَآرِبُ أُخْرى﴾: it has come in the tafsīr: "other needs", and so it is in the language. The singular of "مَآرِب" is "مَأْرُبَةٌ" and "مَأْرَبَةٌ". "أُخْرى" came in the form of the singular feminine adjective because "مَآرِب" has the sense of a collective, so it is as though they are collections of other needs; had "أُخَرُ" come, it would be correct.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ما أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ القُرْآنَ لِتَشْقى﴾, that is: [We did not send it down] so that you should pray on one of your feet and it become hard for you. And it has been said: "طَـهَ" is a word in a foreign (non-Arabic) language, meaning "O man".
As for whoever gives fatḥa to the ṭāʾ and the hāʾ, it is because what precedes the alif is with fatḥa. Whoever gives kasra to the ṭāʾ and the hāʾ inclines it towards kasra (imāla), because the letter [name] ends in a short alif (maqṣūr), and inclination towards kasra predominates in the maqṣūr. Whoever reads "طَـهْ" with the hāʾ quiescent, there are two aspects in it. One of them is that its origin is "طَـأْ" (tread!) with hamza, and the hāʾ was substituted for it, as they said "هِيّاكَ" for "إيّاكَ", and as they said "هَرَقْتُ" for "أرَقْتُ الماءَ" (I poured out the water). It is also possible that it is from "وَطِيَ" with the hamza dropped, so that it is "طَ يا رَجُلُ" (tread, O man), and then the hāʾ was put on it for the pause, and it was said "طَـهْ".

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿سِيرَتَها الأُولى﴾: the meaning of "سِيرَتَها" is "its way", meaning "its form". When people resemble each other you say: "They are of one sīra and one ṭarīqa (way)", meaning that their appearance is one and their likeness is one — even though "اَلسِّيرَةُ" and "اَلطَّرِيقَةُ" originally apply mostly to action; you say: "So-and-so is on the way (ṭarīqa) of so-and-so, and on his sīra", that is: his actions resemble so-and-so's actions. The meaning is: "We shall return it to a staff as it was."
"سِيرَتَها" is accusative by removal of the preposition, the verb having reached it directly; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is "We shall return it to (إلى) its former state"; and when "إلى" was omitted, the verb — namely "سَنُعِيدُها" — reached [it directly] and put it in the accusative.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
And His saying: ﴿واضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إلى جَناحِكَ﴾: a person's "wing" is his upper arm, up to the root of his armpit.
And His saying: ﴿تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ آيَةً أُخْرى﴾: "آيَةً" is accusative because it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a noun in the position of a ḥāl. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "It will come out white, making clear another sign." It is also possible that "آيَةً أُخْرى" is accusative in the sense of "We have given you another sign" or "We shall give you another sign", because when He said ﴿تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ﴾, there was in that an indication that he was being given another sign, so there was no need to mention "آتَيْناكَ" (We have given you), since there is an indication of it in the speech. "آيَةٌ أُخْرى" in the nominative is also permissible, by implying "هَذِهِ آيَةٌ أُخْرى" (this is another sign).

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿واحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِن لِسانِي﴾ ﴿يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي﴾ [Ṭāhā: 28]: it has come in the tafsīr that there was an impediment (رُتَّة) in his tongue, because Pharaoh's wife put a live coal on his tongue. For when he was a child he had seized Pharaoh by the beard, and Pharaoh intended [harm] to him and said: "This is an enemy." So she informed him that he was a child who did not understand, and that her proof of that was that he put a live coal in his mouth; and thus she warded off from him what Pharaoh had intended against him.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿تَنْـزِيلا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الأرْضَ والسَّماواتِ العُلا﴾: the meaning is "We sent it down a sending down (تَنْزِيلًا)" [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. "اَلْعُلى" is the plural of "اَلْعُلْيا" (the highest); one says "سَماءٌ عُلْيا" (a high heaven) and "سَمَواتٌ عُلى" (high heavens), like "اَلْكُبْرى" and "اَلْكُبَرُ".

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلى العَرْشِ اسْتَوى﴾: the preferred [reading] is the nominative; the genitive is permissible as a badal (substitute) for "مَن" [in ﴿مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ﴾]; the meaning [then] is: "a sending down from the Creator of the earth and the heavens, the All-Merciful (الرَّحْمَنِ)", and then He gave information after that, saying: "عَلى العَرْشِ اسْتَوى". They said the meaning of "اِسْتَوى" is "اِسْتَوْلى" (He took possession) — and Allah knows best. What "اِسْتَوى" points to in the language, regarding what He did in the sense of istiwāʾ, is His saying: ﴿لَهُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما وما تَحْتَ الثَّرى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 6]. "اَلثَّرى" in the language is moisture, and what is beneath the earth is moist. It has come in the tafsīr: "وَما تَحْتَ الثَّرى": what is beneath the earth.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالقَوْلِ فَإنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وأخْفى﴾: "اَلسِّرُّ" (the secret) is what you have concealed within yourself, and "أخْفى" (what is more hidden) is what belongs to the Unseen which none knows but Allah.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿لَهُ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾: it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «"Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them (أحْصاها) will enter Paradise."» The interpretation of «"whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise"» is: whoever affirms the oneness of Allah and mentions these most beautiful names, intending by them affirmation of Allah's oneness and His glorification, will enter Paradise. It has come that whoever says "There is no god but Allah" will enter Paradise; this is for one who mentions the name of Allah affirming His oneness by it — so how about one who mentions all His names, intending by them affirmation of His oneness and praise of Him?!

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لِي وزِيرًا مِن أهْلِي﴾ ﴿هارُونَ أخِي﴾ [Ṭāhā: 30]: the accusative of "هارُونَ" may be explained in two ways. One is that "اِجْعَلْ" takes two objects, so the meaning is "Make Hārūn my brother my minister", and "وَزِيرًا" is accusative as a second object. And "هارُونَ" may be a badal (substitute) for His saying "وَزِيرًا", the meaning being: "Appoint for me a minister from my family", and then He substituted "هارُونَ" for "وَزِيرًا". The first view is better. "أخِي" is a naʿt (adjective) of "هارُونَ".
[Translator's note: «أخِي» is an apposition rather than an adjective in later terminology; the source uses «نَعْت».]

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying: ﴿اشْدُدْ بِهِ أزْرِي﴾ ﴿وَأشْرِكْهُ في أمْرِي﴾ [Ṭāhā: 32]: it is read in two ways. [First,] in the sense of "Make my brother a minister, for if You do that, I will strengthen (أشْدُدْ) my back by him" — "أشْدُدْ" as a statement about oneself; and you have kept the doubled letter separate because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of the command — "and I will make him (وَأُشْرِكْهُ) share in my affair". On this it is read: "هارُونَ أخِي أشْدُدْ بِهِ أزْرِي وأُشْرِكْهُ في أمْرِي", with a disjunctive alif (hamzat qaṭʿ) in "أشْدُدْ" and ḍamma on the alif of "وَأُشْرِكْهُ". Whoever reads "هارُونَ أخِي اشْدُدْ بِهِ أزْرِي وأشْرِكْهُ", it is as a supplication; the meaning is: "O Allah, strengthen my back by him and make him share in my affair."

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ مَنَنّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرى﴾: He has explained what that other time was, namely His saying: ﴿إذْ أوْحَيْنا إلى أُمِّكَ ما يُوحى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 38] ﴿أنِ اقْذِفِيهِ في التّابُوتِ﴾ [Ṭāhā: 39], because by this He saved him from being killed, for Pharaoh was slaughtering the sons.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلى عَيْنِي﴾ [Ṭāhā: 39]: they said its meaning is: and that you might be nourished.
As for the meaning of "أزْرِي" (my back/strength): one says "آزَرْتُ فُلانًا عَلى فُلانٍ" when I have helped him against him and strengthened him; and its like is ﴿فَآزَرَهُ فاسْتَغْلَظَ فاسْتَوى عَلى سُوقِهِ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 29]. So its interpretation is: "I will be strengthened by him and seek his help in my affair." As for "اَلْوَزِيرُ" (minister) in the language, its derivation is from "اَلْوَزَرُ", and "اَلْوَزَرُ" is the mountain in which one takes refuge to escape destruction. Likewise "وَزِيرُ الخَلِيفَةِ" (the caliph's minister) means: the one on whom he relies in his affairs and to whose opinion he resorts.
And His saying: ﴿كَلا لا وزَرَ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 11] means: there is nothing in which to take refuge from the command of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَفَتَنّاكَ فُتُونًا﴾: its meaning is: "We tested you with a testing."
And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلى قَدَرٍ يا مُوسى﴾: it has been said in the tafsīr: "at an appointed time"; and it has been said: "at an appointed measure (قَدَر), [in preparation] for My speaking to you."

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿واصْطَنَعْتُكَ لِنَفْسِي﴾: its interpretation is: "I have chosen you to establish My proof, and I have placed you between Me and My creation, so that in addressing [them] on My behalf and conveying from Me you have come to hold the position that I would hold if I addressed them and argued against them."

zajjaj:42-42.t:
﴿وَلا تَنِيا في ذِكْرِي﴾: its meaning is "and do not you two weaken". One says "وَنى، يَنِي، ونْيًا، ووُنِيًّا" when he weakens; and your saying "قَدْ تَوانى فُلانٌ في هَذا الأمْرِ" means: he has slackened in it and weakened.
And His saying: ﴿لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أوْ يَخْشى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 44]: "لَعَلَّ" in the language is hope and expectation; you say "لَعَلِّي أصِيرُ إلى خَيْرٍ", and its meaning is "I hope and expect that I will come to good." Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — addressed His servants with what they understand. The meaning in it, according to Sībawayh, is: "Go, the two of you, in your hope and expectation." Knowledge from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has already encompassed what will be, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — knew that he would neither take heed nor fear; but the proof becomes binding on him only through clarification, establishing it against him, and demonstration. The messengers are sent while they do not know the Unseen and do not know whether they will be accepted or not; they hope and expect to be accepted. The meaning of "لَعَلَّ" is conceived in their own minds, and on that conception the proof is established. Allah's knowledge of what will be is not that by which the proof becomes binding on human beings; were it so, there would be no benefit in the messengers. So the meaning of "لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أوْ يَخْشى" is that on which all the messengers were sent.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّنا نَخافُ أنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنا أوْ أنْ يَطْغى﴾: the meaning of "يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنا" is: he hastens to punish us. One says "قَدْ فَرَطَ مِنهُ أمْرٌ", that is: something hastily issued from him; "قَدْ أفْرَطَ في الشَّيْءِ" when he has gone to excess in the thing; and "قَدْ فَرَطَ في الشَّيْءِ", that is: he fell short. The meaning of all of it is going ahead in the thing, because "اَلْفَرَطُ" in the language is "the one who goes ahead"; and from it is his ﷺ saying: «"I will go ahead of you (فَرَطُكم) to the Pool."»
[Translator's note: «أفْرَطَ في الشَّيْءِ، إذا سَقَطَ فِيهِ» — "سَقَطَ" may be a corruption of "أسْرَفَ" (went to excess); it is rendered in the latter sense.]

zajjaj:47-47.t:
And His saying: ﴿والسَّلامُ عَلى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الهُدى﴾: greeting is not meant by it; its meaning is only that whoever follows guidance is safe from the punishment and wrath of Allah. The proof that it is not a [greeting of] peace is that it is not the beginning of a meeting or of an address.
And the meaning of ﴿فَأْتِياهُ فَقُولا إنّا رَسُولا رَبِّكَ﴾ — He did not say "So they came to him and said to him: We are the two messengers of your Lord", because the speech has indicated that, so it was unnecessary to say in it "so they came to him and said", since His saying ﴿قالَ فَمَن رَبُّكُما يا مُوسى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 49] contains an indication that they came to him and spoke to him.

zajjaj:50-50.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالَ رَبُّنا الَّذِي أعْطى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدى﴾: its meaning is: "He created everything in the form by which it benefits and which is the most suitable form for it, then guided it to its livelihood." It has also been said: "then He guided it to the place from which offspring comes." The first is clearer as an interpretation, but this is possible, because we see the male of animals coming to the female without having seen a male come to a female before him; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — inspired him with that and guided him to the way of approach. The first view encompasses this meaning, because if He guided it to its welfare, this is included in welfare; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قالَ فَما بالُ القُرُونِ الأُولى﴾: Mūsā — peace be upon him — said to him: ﴿عِلْمُها عِنْدَ رَبِّي في كِتابٍ لا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي ولا يَنْسى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 52]; its meaning is: "He does not mislay it nor forget it" — and "My Lord does not mislay it nor forget it", meaning the book.
The meaning of "ضَلَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ" and "ضَلِلْتُ" — with kasra and fatḥa on the lām — "أضِلُّهُ" and "أضَلُّهُ", is: when you have put it in a place and do not know where it is. "يُضِلُّ" is from "أضْلَلْتُهُ", and the meaning of "أضْلَلْتُهُ" is "I lost it."
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: whoever reads with fatḥa [يَضِلُّ], its meaning is "does not go astray", that is: "it does not escape from my Lord"; and if you give the yāʾ ḍamma [يُضِلُّ], its meaning is: "My Lord is not found having lost it."

zajjaj:54-54.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآياتٍ لأُولِي النُّهى﴾: its meaning is: "for those possessed of intellects." The singular of "اَلنُّهى" is "نُهْيَةٌ"; one says "فُلانٌ ذُو نُهْيَةٍ", and its meaning is "possessed of an intellect by which he refrains (يَنْتَهِي) from foul deeds and by which he enters into good ones." Some authorities on the language said: "ذُو النُّهْيَةِ" is the one whose opinion and intellect people end up at (يُنْتَهى إلى); and this is good too.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿مِنها خَلَقْناكم وفِيها نُعِيدُكُمْ﴾: the earth is meant by it, because Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — created Ādam from dust; and the pronoun refers back to His saying: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرْضَ مَهْدًا وسَلَكَ لَكم فِيها سُبُلا﴾ [Ṭāhā: 53].
And His saying: ﴿تارَةً أُخْرى﴾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying "وَمِنها نُخْرِجُكُمْ", because the meaning is like the meaning of the first; for the meaning of "and from it We shall bring you out" is equivalent to "from it We created you", so it is as though He said — and Allah knows best —: "And from it We shall create you another time", because bringing them out while they are dust is equivalent to creating Ādam from dust.
And His saying "مَكانًا سِوًى" — it is also read "سُوًى" with ḍamma — its meaning is: midway, that is: "a place that is half-way between us and you." "سَواءٌ" has also come in the language in this sense; you say "هَذا مَكانٌ سَواءٌ", that is: midway between the two places. But it has only been read with the short form: "سِوًى" and "سُوًى".
[Translator's note: ﴿مَكانًا سُوًى﴾ belongs to Ṭāhā 58; it is discussed here in the source.]

zajjaj:59-59.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قالَ مَوْعِدُكم يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ﴾ — it is also read "يَوْمَ الزِّينَةِ". The nominative is as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the meaning is: "The time of your appointment is the Day of Adornment." Whoever reads "يَوْمَ", it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the meaning being: "It takes place on the Day of Adornment."
And His saying: ﴿وَأنْ يُحْشَرَ النّاسُ ضُحًى﴾: the position of "أنْ" [with its verb] is nominative; the meaning is: "Your appointment is the gathering of the people at forenoon", and its interpretation is: "when you see that the people have been gathered at forenoon." It has been said: "the Day of Adornment" was a festival day they had; and it has been said: it was the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. And it may be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to "اَلزِّينَةِ"; the meaning [then] is: "Your appointment is on the Day of Adornment and the day of the people's gathering."

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالَ لَهم مُوسى ويْلَكم لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾: "وَيْلَكُمْ" is accusative on the sense that Allah has bound woe upon them; and it may be accusative as a vocative, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ [Hūd: 72] and ﴿يا ويْلَنا مَن بَعَثَنا مِن مَرْقَدِنا﴾ [Yā Sīn: 52].
And His saying "فَيَسْحِتَكم بِعَذابٍ" — it is also read "فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ", with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ. One says "سَحَتَهُ" and "أسْحَتَهُ" when he has extirpated and destroyed him. Al-Farazdaq said:
؎وَعَضَّ زَمانٌ يا ابْنَ مَرْوانَ لَمْ يَدَعْ مِنَ المالِ إلّا مُسْحَتًا أوْ مُجَلَّفُ
(And a biting time, O son of Marwān, which left of wealth nothing but what was wiped out or stripped bare.)
The meaning of "لَمْ يَدَعْ" is: nothing of wealth remained settled — from "اَلدَّعَةُ" (rest). Most transmissions have "إلّا مُسْحَتًا", and this is on "أُسْحِتَ، فَهو مُسْحَتٌ" (it was wiped out, so it is wiped out).

zajjaj:62-62.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَتَنازَعُوا أمْرَهم بَيْنَهم وأسَرُّوا النَّجْوى﴾: by this the sorcerers are meant. They said among themselves: "If Mūsā overcomes us, we will believe in him, and the matter will be his."

zajjaj:63-63.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالُوا إنْ هَذانِ لَساحِرانِ﴾: they mean Mūsā and Hārūn. This expression in the Book of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — is difficult for the authorities on the language, and their disagreement over its interpretation has been great. We shall mention everything the grammarians have said, and state what we think is correct; and Allah knows best.
Before explaining its iʿrāb (grammatical analysis), we report the readings of the Quran readers. As for the reading of the people of Medina and the majority in recitation [Translator's note: the source has «والأكْمَهِ», evidently a corruption of «والأكْثَرِ», "the majority"], it is with "إنَّ" doubled and the nominative in "هَذانِ". Likewise the people of Iraq read: Ḥamza, and ʿĀṣim — in the transmission of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh — and the Medinans.
It is related from ʿĀṣim: "إنْ هَذانِ", with "إنْ" lightened. What ʿĀṣim read in this reading is confirmed by what is related from Ubayy, for he read: "ما هَذانِ إلّا ساحِرانِ" (these two are nothing but two sorcerers); and it is also related from him that he read: "إنْ هَذانِ إلّا ساحِرانِ". It has also been related from al-Khalīl: "إنْ هَذانِ لَساحِرانِ", with the light form; and there is consensus that no one was more learned in grammar than al-Khalīl. Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read: "إنَّ هَذَيْنِ لَساحِرانِ", with "إنَّ" doubled and "هَذَيْنِ" in the accusative.
This is the transmission concerning it. As for the grammarians' argumentation: Abū ʿAmr's argument for departing from the muṣḥaf in this is that it was related that it is a scribe's error, and that in the written text there is an error which the Arabs will set right with their tongues; that is related from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and from ʿĀʾisha — may Allah have mercy on them both.
As for the argument for "إنَّ هَذانِ", with "إنَّ" doubled and "هَذانِ" in the nominative: Abū ʿUbayda reported from Abū al-Khaṭṭāb — who was one of the leading transmitters — that it is a dialect of Kināna, who keep the alif of the dual in one form in the nominative, accusative and genitive. They say: "أتانِي الزَّيْدانِ" (the two Zayds came to me), "رَأيْتُ الزَّيْدانِ" (I saw the two Zayds) and "مَرَرْتُ بِالزَّيْدانِ" (I passed by the two Zayds). And these people recite:
؎فَأطْرَقَ إطْراقَ الشُّجاعِ ولَوْ رَأى مَساغًا لِناباهُ الشُّجاعُ لَصَمَّما
(He lay low as the serpent lies low; and had the serpent seen room for its two fangs, it would have bitten deep.)
These people also say "ضَرَبْتُهُ بَيْنَ أُذُناهُ" (I struck him between his two ears) and "مَن يَشْتَرِي مِنِّي الخُفّانِ؟" (who will buy the two boots from me?). Likewise the people of Kufa related that it is a dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb.
The early grammarians said: there is an implied hāʾ here [the pronoun of the matter, ḍamīr al-shaʾn]; the meaning is: "إنَّهُ هَذانِ لَساحِرانِ" (it is [the case that] these two are sorcerers). They also said: the meaning of "إنْ" [here] is the meaning of "نَعَمْ" (yes); the meaning is: "Yes, these two are sorcerers." And they recite:
؎وَيَقُلْنَ شَيْبٌ قَدْ عَلا ∗∗∗ كَ وقَدْ كَبِرْتَ فَقُلْتُ إنَّهْ
(They [the women] say: grey hair has come over you, and you have grown old; and I said: yes (إنَّهْ).)
And they argue that the original place of this lām is at the beginning [of the nominal sentence], but that its occurrence in the khabar (predicate) is permissible, and they recite for this:
؎خالِي لَأنْتَ ومَن جَرِيرٌ خالُهُ ∗∗∗ يَنَلِ العَلاءَ ويُكْرِمِ الإخْوانا
(My maternal uncle — you indeed are; and whoever has Jarīr for a maternal uncle attains eminence and is generous to his brothers.)
And they also recited:
؎أُمُّ الحُلَيْسِ لَعَجُوزٌ شَهْرَبَةْ ∗∗∗ تَرْضى مِنَ الشّاةِ بِعَظْمِ الرَّقَبَةْ
(Umm al-Ḥulays is indeed a decrepit old woman, who is content with the neck-bone of the sheep.)
They said: the meaning is "لَأنْتَ خالِي" (you indeed are my uncle), and the meaning is "لَأُمُّ الحُلَيْسِ عَجُوزٌ" (Umm al-Ḥulays indeed is an old woman).
Al-Farrāʾ said about this: they added the nūn in the dual and left the alif as it was in the nominative, accusative and genitive, just as they did with "اَلَّذِي", saying "اَلَّذِينَ" in the nominative, accusative and genitive.
This is all that the grammarians have argued. What I hold — and Allah knows best — and I had presented it to our two learned men, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] and the judge Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq ibn Ḥammād ibn Zayd, and they accepted it and said it was the best they had heard on this, is: "إنْ" [i.e. "إنَّ"] has occurred in the place of "نَعَمْ" (yes), and the lām has occurred in its proper place, and the meaning is: "هَذانِ لَهُما ساحِرانِ" (these two — they are indeed two sorcerers) [i.e. with an omitted mubtadaʾ "هُما" after the lām].
What comes next to this in quality is the way of Banū Kināna in keeping the alif of the dual in one form, because the alif's due is to indicate the dual, and its due was not to change, just as the alif of "رَحًى" (millstone) and "عَصًا" (staff) does not change; but changing it to yāʾ in the accusative and genitive was clearer and better for distinguishing the nominative, the accusative and the genitive.
As for the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, I do not permit it, because it goes against the muṣḥaf; and whatever I find closer to agreement with the muṣḥaf, I do not permit departing from it, because following it is a sunna, and it is what most of the readers hold. But I consider "إنْ هَذانِ لَساحِرانِ", with "إنْ" lightened, good; there are two authorities for it, ʿĀṣim and al-Khalīl, and it agrees with Ubayy in meaning, even if it differs from him in wording.
"إنَّ هَذانِ" with the doubled form is also considered good, because it is the way of most of the readers, it is what is recited, and it is strong in Arabic.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَذْهَبا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ المُثْلى﴾: its meaning, according to the grammarians, is "your noble company". "اَلْمُثْلى" is the feminine of "اَلْأمْثَلُ", and the meaning of "اَلْأمْثَلُ" and "اَلْمُثْلى" is "one possessed of excellence who deserves that it be said of him: this is the best (أمْثَلُ) of his people." In the tafsīr: "بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ المُثْلى": your nobles.
The Arabs say of an excellent man: "هَذا طَرِيقَةُ قَوْمِهِ" (this is the ṭarīqa of his people), "نَظِيرَةُ قَوْمِهِ" and "نَظُورَةُ قَوْمِهِ"; all of these are for the excellent man. Its interpretation is only: "This is the one whom his people ought to take as an example and whose way (ṭarīqa) they ought to follow." And as for the one who also said "هَذا نَظُورَةُ قَوْمِهِ" and "نَظِيرَةُ قَوْمِهِ", its meaning is: "This is the one to whom his people ought to look and whom they ought to follow."
What I hold — and Allah knows best — is that there is an omission in the speech indicated by what remains; the meaning is only: "and they will take away the people of your exemplary way", as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنّا فِيها﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], meaning "and ask the people of the town." Likewise the Arabs' saying "هَذا طَرِيقَةُ قَوْمِهِ" means: "This is the possessor of the way of his people."

zajjaj:64-64.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَأجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ﴾ — it has also been read "فاجْمَعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ". Whoever reads "فَأجْمِعُوا", with a disjunctive alif (hamzat qaṭʿ), its meaning is: "Let the resolve of all of you be agreed upon the plot", that is: "Do not differ, lest you fall into disorder." Whoever reads "فاجْمَعُوا", its meaning is: "Bring every plot you are capable of, and leave nothing of it out."
And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا﴾: its meaning is: "Come to the place where you gather for your festival and your prayer"; one says "أتَيْتُ صَفًّا" in the sense of "I came to the place of prayer." And "ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا" may mean: "Then come in ranks, gathered together, so that it is more orderly for your affairs and more imposing in your appearance." ﴿وَقَدْ أفْلَحَ اليَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلى﴾: the meaning of "مَنِ اسْتَعْلى" is: whoever rises above by prevailing.

zajjaj:66-66.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قالَ بَلْ ألْقُوا فَإذا حِبالُهم وعِصِيُّهُمْ﴾: He did not say here "so they threw, and behold, their ropes…", because it has come in another place: ﴿فَألْقَوْا حِبالَهم وعِصِيَّهُمْ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 44]. In "عِصِيٌّ" "عُصِيٌّ" is permissible; the kasra is more common, and the original is the ḍamma, but [ḍamma followed by] kasra is heavy after ḍamma, and so kasra of the ʿayn [i.e. first letter] was preferred.
It is related in the tafsīr that the sorcerers on that day were seventy thousand sorcerers, with seventy thousand ropes and seventy thousand staffs. When it seemed to him from their sorcery that they were moving, Allah revealed to Mūsā that he should throw his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent with its mouth gaping, and it swallowed all those ropes.
And it has been read: ﴿فَإذا حِبالُهم وعِصِيُّهم يُخَيَّلُ إلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أنَّها تَسْعى﴾. The position of "أنَّ" on this reading is nominative; the meaning is: "their moving was made to seem to him." It is also read "تُخَيَّلُ", with tāʾ; and on this reading the position of "أنَّ" may be accusative, or it may be nominative. The accusative is in the sense of "they were made to seem to him to be moving"; and it may be nominative as a badal (substitute), in the sense of "their moving was made to seem to him", "أنَّها تَسْعى" being substituted for the pronoun implied in "تُخَيَّلُ" because it comprises its meaning [badal ishtimāl], and "إلَيْهِ" would be the khabar on this analysis. Its like is what Sībawayh reported; one says "ما لِي بِهِمْ عِلْمُ أمْرِهِمْ", that is: "I have no knowledge of their affair." Its like in poetry:
؎وَذَكَرْتُ تَقْتَدَ بَرْدَ مائِها
(And I remembered Taqtad — the coolness of its water.)
The meaning is: "And I remembered the coolness of the water of Taqtad."
[Translator's note: «إلّا أنَّ الكَسْرَ يَثْقُلُ بَعْدَ الضَّمِّ» is as in the source; the sense is that the sequence ḍamma–kasra (عُصِيّ) is heavy, so the first letter was harmonised to kasra.]

zajjaj:67-67.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَأوْجَسَ في نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسى﴾: its original form is "خِوْفَةً", but the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. ﴿وَألْقِ ما في يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ ما صَنَعُوا﴾ [Ṭāhā: 69]: "تَلْقَفْ" — the reading is with the jussive, as the apodosis (jawāb) of the command. The nominative is permissible in the sense of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He said: "Throw it, swallowing [them] up, in an anticipated state"; but it has not been read so, and one ought not recite what has no precedent of reading.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّما صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ ساحِرٍ﴾ — it is also read "كَيْدُ سِحْرٍ" (the plot of sorcery). "أنَّما صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ ساحِرٍ" is permissible, and "كَيْدَ ساحِرٍ" with the dāl in the accusative is permissible. Whoever reads "أنَّما" puts "أنَّما" in the accusative [position] in the sense of "it will swallow up what they made, because what they made is the plot of a sorcerer"; but I know of no one who read it "أنَّما" here. The reading is with kasra, and it is more eloquent in meaning.
As for the nominative of "كَيْدُ", it is in the sense of "Indeed, what they made is the plot of a sorcerer", as the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ", with "ما" a noun [i.e. a relative noun]. Whoever reads "كَيْدَ ساحِرٍ" makes "ما" prevent "إنَّ" from governing and allow a verb to come after it, and "كَيْدَ ساحِرٍ" is accusative by "صَنَعُوا", just as you say "إنَّما ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا" (I only struck Zayd).
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا يُفْلِحُ السّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أتى﴾: they said its meaning is "wherever he is". And it has been said its meaning is: "wherever the sorcerer is, he must be killed"; and that is likewise the doctrine of the jurists concerning sorcerers.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا﴾: "سُجَّدًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it too is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because they fell down while not [yet] prostrating; they only fell down intending prostration.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾: its meaning is "on (عَلى) the trunks of the palm trees"; but "فِي" (in) was permissible here because he is on the trunk lengthwise, and the trunk encloses him, so he has come to be in it. The poet said:
؎وَهم صَلَبُوا العَبْدِيَّ في جِذْعِ نَخْلَةٍ فَلا عَطَسَتْ شَيْبانُ إلّا بِأجْدَعا
(They crucified the man of ʿAbd [al-Qays] on (in) the trunk of a palm tree; so may Shaybān never sneeze except with a cut-off nose.)
His saying: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أيُّنا أشَدُّ عَذابًا وأبْقى﴾: "أيُّ" is in the nominative because it has been put in the position of the interrogative, and what precedes "أيُّ" does not govern it, because what precedes it is a statement while it is an interrogative. If it governed it, it would be permissible for it to govern what comes after the alif [of interrogation] in your saying "قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أزَيْدٌ في الدّارِ أمْ عَمْرٌو" (I know whether Zayd is in the house or ʿAmr).
